title: Dig straight down from Madrid
hook: Everyone says you'd come out in China. Pick a spot and find the real other end.

knows: that "digging to China" is a joke
that places have a latitude and a longitude
doesNotKnow: where the point straight through the Earth really is
that most land has ocean on the other side

misconception: Digging straight down from anywhere in the Americas or Europe comes out in China or Asia.
objective: The learner can find an antipode by flipping the latitude's hemisphere and moving 180 degrees of longitude, and can say that most land is opposite ocean.

claims.text: The point straight through the Earth's centre has the same latitude in the other hemisphere and a longitude 180 degrees away.
claims.source: On a sphere the antipode of (lat, lon) is (-lat, lon +/- 180). Geodetic latitude on the ellipsoid gives the same rule (the ellipsoid is symmetric through its centre).

claims.text: Madrid (40.42 N, 3.70 W) is opposite 40.42 S, 176.30 E, which is in New Zealand.
claims.source: geoContains on the kit's 1:110m New Zealand shape is true at (176.30 E, 40.42 S) (scratch a.mjs, 2026-10-13). Madrid coordinates from memory of a gazetteer (GeoNames: 40.4165 N, 3.7026 W), not checked online. The point is near the east coast of the North Island, so the lesson names no town and does not say inland.

claims.text: On this map only about 13% of the land sits opposite other land.
claims.source: 1 degree grid of the kit's 1:110m land polygon, cell-weighted by cos(latitude): 13.3% of land has land at its antipode (3.9% of the whole surface). Published figures are about 15% of land, about 4.4% of the surface (Wikipedia, 'Antipodes'; not checked online). Resolution shifts this by a few points, hence 'about' and 'on this map'.

claims.text: Almost all of the United States is opposite open ocean, mostly the Indian Ocean.
claims.source: 1 degree cells inside the 1:110m 'United States of America' shape: 99.3% have an ocean antipode, 0.6% Antarctica (from Alaska), 0.1% Botswana (from Hawaii). The contiguous states map to about 25-49 S, 55-113 E, the southern Indian Ocean (ocean name from the coordinates; not a data lookup).

claims.text: About three-quarters of China is opposite ocean; the rest is opposite Argentina and Chile.
claims.source: 1 degree cells inside the 1:110m 'China' shape, area-weighted: 72.7% ocean antipode, Argentina 22.3%, Chile 4.8%, others under 0.5% (scratch d.mjs, 2026-10-13).

claims.text: Beijing is opposite Argentina, Buenos Aires is opposite sea off China, and New York is opposite the Indian Ocean (stage readouts).
claims.source: Computed live on the stage with geoContains on 1:110m shapes; city coordinates from memory of a gazetteer (Beijing 39.90 N 116.40 E, Buenos Aires 34.60 S 58.38 W, New York 40.71 N 74.00 W), not checked online.

recall.question: A town is at 30 N, 100 W. Where is the point straight through the Earth from it?
recall.why: Flip the latitude to the other hemisphere (30 S) and move 180 degrees of longitude: 100 W plus 180 is 80 E.
